outcome.technical: (1) ONE TABLE. plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_floor_guard.py: _REASONS and _MARKING_DECORATORS are gone; SKIP_FORMS holds each skip, expected failure and mark as (name in its module, the module or * for any receiver, whether it is a decorator that only marks, reason position, reason keywords). _reason_of(call, imported) and _marks_only(decorator, imported) both ask it through _skip_form, which reads the spelling through the copy's imports (_imported, _spelling): a dotted name has its first name replaced by what the copy imports under it, or is read as written when the copy imports nothing under it. A bare name is a row's only when the copy imports it by name from the row's module, an alias included. A name the copy imports from two places, or also defines as a function or class, belongs to nobody. _reason_aside builds the import map once per parse. (2) SAME-FILE BASES. Two new rows in _CLASS_COMPUTED: 'a base class of the copy binding names by computation' (_bound_base) and 'a base class the copy binds more than once' (_rebound_base, which declines rather than guesses). _bases accepts only a bare-name base that the copy defines once as a class and binds no other way; a base spelled through an attribute (mod.Base) is read as another module's. Classes are asked in source order after the own forms and the setattr-pointed classes are noted. A base can be named only once it is bound, and a class nested in a function holds no bare unit, so each class is asked once and the cost is linear in classes plus bases. A base-first DFS (_bases_first) was written and then removed: on any input that can run it gave the same answers as source order, and the probe's ordering row could not tell them apart. The transitive closure of subclass hooks is gone too: a metaclass on a base and a hook reached through a further base are now read by the base row. (3) HANDED NAMESPACE. New _COMPUTED row 'a namespace handed to a callee the copy defines' (_namespace_handed, _file_callee). The copy defines the callee when the name is a function, class, method or lambda assigned to a name at any depth (_copy_facts callees). A method reached through a name the copy imports is not the copy's. The callee's body is not read: handing it the namespace is the binding. (4) ROWS CARRY EXAMPLES. Every row of _COMPUTED and _CLASS_COMPUTED is (what, function, examples), each example a base copy plus a bare test appended to it. BINDINGS is the pair. Every form now takes (node, facts). find_moves takes a trailing bindings=None, passed down through _one_file, _collect, _python_test, _new_test_aside and _computed_scopes; drive-phase.py calls it with five positional arguments and is unchanged. fx10 runs each example through find_moves twice: with BINDINGS, where it must be partly-read with one notRead naming '(<row>, at line'; and with a tuple missing that row, where it must be clean. A row with no example, or whose example reads the same without it, fails by name. The equivalent row _module_attribute_store is removed (an attribute store always spells the name, which _identifiers already reads). fx10 found no other equivalent row and no row without an example. (5) ORACLE. tests/test__floor_guard.py: before, _inv_binds counted a namespace handed to ANY call as binding, and _inv_bound read dotted marks only, with no bases and no pointed setattr. Now the oracle has its own import reading (_inv_imports, _inv_resolve); INV_REASONS holds only canonical names (INV_MARKS, INV_MARK_FAMILY). A namespace counts only when handed to a callee the copy defines; module-wide globals()/sys.modules forms bind the module from anywhere; setattr points at a named class; a class is bound through same-file bases (memoised), a hook base, a metaclass, a non-marking decorator, or a base bound twice. _InvAside now takes the copy's imports. It imports none of the module's tables. fx11 checks it against every row example (bound) and against the allow twins of fa57 and fa59 (set aside); fx4 and fx9 are unchanged and green. (6) DOCS. plugins/audit/README.md (floorGuard.mode row) and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (_floor_guard.py section) name every row by its own words. The list of what is knowingly not read is one paragraph, in the guide alone; README, CHANGELOG and the module docstring point to it. fx12 checks that README and guide name every row (backticks stripped, whitespace folded) and that the not-read marker phrase appears in the guide only. CHANGELOG.md has a new Unreleased bullet. tools/gate-parity.py is not touched: SKIP_FORMS is not a reason-carrying exemption table. NEW CASES: fa57, fa58, fm80, fm81, fm82, fa59, fx10, fx11, fx12. EXISTING CASES CHANGED ON PURPOSE: none of their assertions; only the oracle helpers they call (_inv_reason_spec, _inv_binds, _inv_bound, _InvAside, _inv_own, _inv_dump, _inv_copy) and one import line (REPO_ROOT, os). outcome.descriptive: The floor guard reads a skip or a mark through one table and the file's imports, so bare-spelled skips and marks read clean again. It reads a class with its same-file bases and reads a namespace handed to a same-file helper. Every binding-table row now carries examples that one case runs with the row and without it.
